items.title: Harold Danko interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 28, 2021
items.q: I knew his Five by Five, the Monk records that he did and also what he did early on with Mingus, “The Jazz Experiments of Charles Mingus”

ctx.x: So it was a horrible Fender Rhodes but it was in residence there so I did a lot of gigs at Striker’s. So that was very good for me, and a lot of people do remember that club because it was pretty intimate and you know it was a chance to go hear Lee Konitz in a trio and he was pretty low profile at that point. You know I mean he was, well it was before he formed the nonet. And that was, he started getting some ideas about re- asserting himself on the scene I think, but he was not doing a whole lot other than these…

looking for somebody for the band.” You know and I was like, and I truthfully didn’t know a whole lot about the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band. I knew Thad as a player. I knew his Five by Five, the Monk records that he did and also what he did early on with Mingus, “The Jazz Experiments of Charles Mingus” where you know, so I knew Thad’s playing. I didn’t really know his writing, but I guess I comped in the places that was good — so anyway I had a shot to do the big band and Mel Lewis gave me a heads up on what charts…
